body:
I wonder if that's better. We do now see multiple files (good).

But first reaction is why "commons-chunk"? (I get it but the users?).

Then you look at the code and see:

![2015-10-09-103249_1155x272_scrot](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/123822/10389369/28eaf5ee-6e71-11e5-99bc-04e4dc157a39.png)

For me it's trying to show the user that the code is readable while it's not very readable and it will just raise the FUD around it.

I would no tackle this for now, it's not a big deal if we have good documentation on how to use instantsearch.js.

Users really wanting to know how the example works can just have a look at the source code.

The instantsearch demo will be the tutorial we show to users, not the example app of instantsearch.js which should be used as a `dev` tool and not something we want our users to fully understand.

The instant search demo port using instantsearch.js will be the entry point for our users to understand how to build such UI.
